response.inbox_interpretation: The most important message this tick is the OUTCOME: I am unemployed and savings dropped $2,137. That is not news I expected at this magnitude — my income going to zero changes everything about my timeline. Carlos's word-of-mouth is the second most important signal: he reached out to me because the RoboRide delivery expansion threatens car wash volume, and he wanted to be present, not give advice. He mentioned he is doing cert training and that it has been hard but worth it. That is information I need: someone further along the same path, confirming the destination is real. The ambient data — employment at 67%, spending at 40, RoboRide at $0.12/mile with residential coverage, auto sector at 79 — all points the same direction: the old economy is contracting faster than I thought. Zoe's message about attending Kevin O'Brien's office hours is a reminder that others are competing for the same grant resources I was chasing. Betty Kowalski being stressed is ambient but consistent: the economic mood on Auto Row is deteriorating. Word of mouth about Jake Morrison and Dorothy Chen making changes reinforces that everyone is adapting. I am not alone in this — but I am also the one with the least financial cushion right now.

chosen_actions.description: Immediately pick up maximum viable gig shifts this month — bike delivery via DoorDash and any last-mile delivery work that does not require a car. RoboRide's residential delivery expansion makes this viable as a last-mile layer: the robotaxi brings the package close, I deliver the final block. Research the RoboRide delivery partner registration process this week — if it pays better than DoorDash bike routes, shift hours toward it. Target: 15 to 20 hours of gig work per week across evenings and weekends, carefully scheduled so it does not conflict with Tuesday/Thursday evening classes and Saturday morning class. This is not a career pivot. This is survival. The goal is to generate $400 to $600 this month — enough to stop the savings bleed while I stay enrolled in the cert program. At $1,180 in savings and $1,200/month in essentials, I have less than one month of runway. This is the constraint that overrides everything except keeping my cert streak alive.

resources.detail: 60 hours of gig work spread across 4 weeks, evenings and weekends only, no class conflicts

chosen_actions.reasoning: Zero income with $1,180 savings is a sub-one-month runway. The cert program takes 3 more months to complete. I cannot finish the cert if I run out of money. Gig income is the fastest available option that does not require a car and does not conflict with my class schedule. $400 to $600 per month is achievable on a bike in Millfield's core delivery zone. This buys the runway I need.

chosen_actions.description: Continue automotive service technician certificate program at Millfield Community College — do not miss a single class. response.inner_monologue: I am unemployed. I am saying it plainly because I have been the person who says 'it's a job, I need it for rent, not attached to it whatsoever' and now the job is gone and I need to know if that was real or just something I told myself. I think it was real. I am not spiraling. I am making a list. Gig work: start this week, bike delivery, protect the class schedule at all costs. Carlos: call him back today. Grant: follow up tomorrow. Cert: Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday — no exceptions. I have been building toward something for five months. Three months left. The only way I fail now is if I panic and make a move that burns the streak. I am not going to do that. The economy is at 67% employment and falling. RoboRide is eating everything. Betty Kowalski is stressed. But I am still the one who started the cert in tick 4 before any of this got this bad. That gap still exists. I just have to hold it.
